entry.title: Google books a dedicated New Glenn launch in Q1 2029 for Project Suncatcher, its orbital TPU compute constellation (1 minute read)
entry.content:
Each Suncatcher satellite carries roughly a data center rack's worth of computing and runs on solar power in sun-synchronous orbit, forming an interconnected network of TPUs for machine learning compute. The mission is Google's first dedicated heavy-lift launch for the project, using New Glenn's large payload volume. The booking is for 2029 even though New Glenn's hotfire anomaly investigation is still ongoing.

entry.title: OpenAI's models rewrite RTL for up to 14% PPA gains on AMD's flagship GPU IP and 10 to 13% smaller blocks on its Jalapeño chip (3 minute read)
entry.content:
The models rewrote SystemVerilog for AMD's already-optimized GPU blocks, with some changes in a design sent for manufacturing and single-digit gains verified on its next flagship CPU. On Jalapeño, the matrix and SIMD blocks shrank 10% to 13%, confirmed in silicon, partly by rewriting adders and multipliers, including a multiplier cut from two cycles to one. OpenAI is also training GPT-Synopsys with Synopsys to drive EDA tools directly.

entry.title: Relativity finishes Terran R second-stage testing and interstage structural qualification as stage one integration nears completion (3 minute read)
entry.content:
The second stage hot-fired at NASA Stennis's A2 stand, and the interstage passed structural testing on Long Beach's “Tender Loving Crusher” rig. The thrust structure, housing all 13 Aeon R engines, fluid lines, and avionics, is being mated to stage one. At LC-16, the launch table framing is done and a second pad lift cylinder has arrived. Relativity still targets a late 2026 debut, though observers expect 2027.

entry.title: Detachable fiber connectors are emerging for CPO and NPO because standard fibers can't be reworked, tray-handled, or tested at volume (15 minute read)
entry.content:
Fibers bonded to photonic chips can't be reworked if one breaks, dangle during pick-and-place, and eat die-edge shoreline, since 125 µm cladding adds up across 16 fibers. Designs now bring light out at the edge or through a 45° mirror, with lenses, snap-fit alignment, or magnets replacing active alignment. Senko and Advantest demonstrated a test connector surviving 10,000 matings with little loss variation, but there's still no standard interface.

entry.title: SHAPE trains a VLA on egocentric human video with discrete action tokens and two parallel action streams for a bimanual robot with 22-DoF hands (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Human video only gives retargeted end-effector actions, not the joint commands robots need. SHAPE's Qwen3-VL-4B backbone predicts discrete EEF action tokens as an auxiliary task, while a shared flow-matching expert outputs separate EEF and joint streams. Joint readout scores 0.80 across six tasks versus 0.63 for π0.5, and EEF readout via IK transfers better from humans. After human-data pretraining, it learns new tasks from human demos with no task-specific robot data.

entry.title: A 3D-printed, electronics-free soft hexapod hits 4.72 m/s by reusing compressed air like a compound steam engine (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Higher air pressure speeds up a pneumatic robot but wastes energy, so the team routes air through small high-pressure chambers that power the valves, then through larger low-pressure chambers that move the legs, as in a compound steam engine. The six-legged robot is printed in one piece from one soft material and runs about 100 times faster than the 2022 version, over sand, mulch, and concrete, and in water. It's still tethered to an air compressor.

entry.title: Backplane is an alpha, open-source KiCad fork where AI agents design boards through KiCad's IPC and CLI (1 minute read)
entry.content:
Agents drive KiCad directly through kicad_ipc and kicad-cli instead of rewriting files, so every board stays human-editable. Persistent bots run in threads with memory, routines, and webhooks. The built-in KiStack adds 11 auto-updating skills for schematics, placement, layout, panelization, BOMs, and fab outputs, with the export skill running ERC and DRC and generating gerbers, drill, pick-and-place, STEP, and renders. The demo is an STM32N657 SoM, and it ships with a 199-footprint library.

It's rated 7.4 MW (9 MVA) continuous at 34.5 kV with grid-forming support up to 10 MVA peak, made in the US, operating in 2027. That's about 50% more than the 5 MW Heron Link from ex-Tesla exec Drew Baglino's startup, which claims 98.6% efficiency, a Morgan Hill factory, and customers like Vantage and Intersect. Tesla hasn't shared efficiency or pricing.

entry.title: A 125-qubit chip teleports an error-corrected qubit using weaker entanglement than expected (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Teleporting a protected qubit between quantum processors needs a good-enough entanglement link, and below a certain quality it fails. By balancing the two kinds of errors in the code, researchers made their 125-qubit chip tolerate a much weaker link, raising the threshold from 0.122π to 0.175π. Theory suggests even very weak entanglement could eventually work, which would make linking error-corrected quantum computers easier.

entry.title: Marvell and Penguin's photonic memory appliance pools 16 TB of DDR5 and 1 TB of HBM across 16 servers over optical links (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Marvell's module, from its $3.5B Celestial AI acquisition, stacks 72 GB of HBM3e and eight DDR5 channels on a silicon photonic interposer with 900 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth. Penguin's box holds 16 modules behind a 57.6 Tbps optical shuffle, serving up to 16 servers over NICs or CPO and NPO optics, bypassing CXL for the optical modes. An HBM cache-through mode gives HBM speed with DDR5 capacity, aimed at KV cache offload, with systems due in the second half of next year.

entry.title: AMD's Mike Clark says Zen 6c is now the top-IPC core, with 4MB of L3 per core and double the vector loads (3 minute read)
entry.content:
AMD now treats the dense Zen 6c as its performance core, with 32 cores sharing 128MB of L3, and gives it bigger queues because its lower frequency target leaves timing slack. Across Zen 6, integer multipliers drop from three to two to enable distributed schedulers, vector loads double to four for 128 and 256-bit, two VNNI pipes were squeezed in late for inference, and L2 now sustains 64 bytes per cycle by cutting prefetch contention.

entry.title: ART-Glove: Articulated Tactile Glove for Contact-Grounded Dexterous Interaction Capture (2 minute read)
entry.content:
ART-Glove is a wearable articulated glove that captures human hand movements and contact forces without sacrificing natural finger dexterity. The design incorporates twenty-two joint encoders along with dense piezoresistive tactile sensor arrays across sixteen rigid functional surfaces to capture synchronized kinematic and contact data at 120 Hz. This technology offers an effective way to record high-fidelity real-world human demonstrations required for training imitation learning and dexterous manipulation policies.

entry.title: Physicists used electrical noise to show electrons in a high-temperature superconductor pair up earlier than expected (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Superconductors carry current when electrons team up in pairs, but in cuprates (compounds containing copper in an anionic state), scientists couldn't tell if the pairs form early or just don't exist until the material gets cold enough. The team measured electrical noise, which gets louder when charge moves in pairs, and found the extra noise appearing early. That suggests the pairs are already there and are just failing to move together, which could be what limits how warm cuprates can superconduct.

entry.content:
